analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only: scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py, scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py and the metadata of scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py (no text supplied). None change shipped provider, coordinator or cryptographic code, so no regression against the provider threat model (T-041 prefix cache, TB-009 attestation, TB-011 App Attest and similar) is evident.

The tests encode a release-policy change:
- Master pushes publish staging only. A master push routed to dev or prod fails closed.
- A dev-branch push publishes dev only, with version -dev.branch.N. Staging or prod routed from a dev push fails closed. Only refs/heads/dev is accepted.
- A dispatched dev lane resolves only as an unpublished validation build. A dev publication without a dev push is refused.
- verify_workflow_source, in provider_release_resume/api.py (not supplied), is tested to require a GitHub-verified commit and dev ancestry through git/ref/heads/dev plus compare, with environment dev. Dev ancestry must not satisfy a master-route check.
- Malformed or injected env values (newlines, $(…)) still emit no outputs.

The tests are consistent and fail-closed. The security-relevant new surface is the dev-push path. The dev lane now Developer ID-signs, notarizes and publishes builds from pushes to dev, per the description in test-release-dev-branch.py. Whether the real resolve-provider-release.sh, provider_release_resume/api.py and release-dev-branch.yml match these tests is unverified. Open points to check:
- Branch protection on dev, including required signed commits and review.
- That the dev caller cannot reach prod or staging secrets.
- That the publication concurrency and the DEV_RELEASE_KEY scoping hold.
- That a dev-signed build cannot be accepted by production allowlists or qualifications (A-011, A-017, T-054).
These are outside the supplied evidence, so I record them as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
